tasks.short: Develop security threat detection, prevention and analysis tools.

steps.what: Define threat scenarios, safe boundaries and independent acceptance cases
Develop software tools in an isolated branch

loop.purpose: Draft a bounded implementation of the specified security tool
loop.input: Accepted specification and authorised repository context
loop.check: Run independent benign and malicious fixtures; engineer reviews detection logic, privilege scope and unsafe behaviour
loop.stop: Two unsuccessful attempts or any requirement ambiguity returns the diff to manual development
loop.why_not_simpler: Threat-specific parsing and detection logic do not reduce to a fixed template; try native detection rules first

steps.what: Execute isolated tests against the candidate tool
Review code, failures and operational limits; approve the final deployment package
Commit the approved security tool release
Deploy the committed approved security tool release
Check live behaviour and record acceptance or rollback decision
Save the checked rollout decision

tasks.design: Use the native rule engine before custom code. Where custom logic remains, draft a bounded branch in {OTHER}, the isolated repository and test environment. Configure its test runner and release pipeline. Keep threat modelling, independent fixtures, final code review and live acceptance human. Commit and deploy are separate gated release actions; save the rollout decision separately.
tasks.previous_blocker: Threat-specific code needs security context and meaningful tests, not just syntactically valid output.
tasks.enabler_now: Repository-scoped drafting and native test runners can assist implementation without production credentials.
tasks.still_hard: Coverage gaps, evasion, false positives and excessive privileges remain engineering judgements.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which threats matter and decide whether the complete tool is safe to operate.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time on first-pass implementation and repeated test launches.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: isolated code drafting and existing CI test runners can support security-tool development; no local saving is measured.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for a custom-tool change, not measured effort. Baseline includes only hands-on test execution and release operations; existing CI runtime earns no saving.

s1 engineer supplies requirement_id, threat_scenario, expected_outcome, fixture_id, allowed_inputs, privilege_scope and rollback_target. Fixture creation stays fully counted. Missing fixtures or repository access means manual development.
s2 retained time includes context selection, reading and repairing generated code. s4 retains full substantive review. Native rule configuration is evaluated before custom generation.

a1 and a3 bind the final diff hash, test results, environment and rollback target after s4. Edited code invalidates approval. Production actions have no model authority. A rollback requires its own approved action outside this successful-release path.
s6 engineer records deployed_hash, observed_result and accept_or_rollback; s7 is a separate manual save approved on the finished note. No new log automation saving is assumed.
research_questions: Which actual hands-on implementation and test-launch actions remain after native detection rules and existing CI?

incremental.description: Maintain isolated drafting context and test-runner integration

approvals.approved_version: s4 final release hash and repository target
s4 final release hash, deployment target and rollback package

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 10.5 coding, 10 test-launch and 5 release hours, less 2 upkeep = 23.5. Low retains existing test/release automation and gets coding benefit only: 10.5 minus 2 = 8.5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write reports on security breaches and network evaluations.

steps.what: Select verified investigation evidence and determine disclosure limits
Assemble factual event tables with source references
Determine supported conclusions, uncertainty and corrective recommendations
Write reports from the engineer's conclusions and cited evidence

loop.purpose: Draft report prose without inferring new facts or attribution
loop.input: Engineer conclusions, cited tables and audience restrictions
loop.output: Candidate report with claim-level evidence pointers
loop.check: Engineer verifies causality, chronology, uncertainty and sensitive details against the actual evidence
loop.stop: Unsupported conclusion or two failed revisions returns the affected section to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Case-specific explanatory prose exceeds fixed factual table templates

steps.what: Approve the final report, redactions and recipient list
File the approved security report
Send the approved report link to approved internal recipients

tasks.design: Use a native report export or a deterministic mapping from the authorised incident store in {OTHER} into {DOCS}. Keep conclusions human. Bounded drafting turns those conclusions into prose; the final complete redacted version and recipients are reviewed before separate filing and {EMAIL} delivery steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Investigation evidence and audience-specific explanations are not interchangeable.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured case exports can populate factual tables, while source-scoped drafting can assist explanatory writing.
tasks.still_hard: Causality, attribution, uncertainty and disclosure decisions require an accountable investigator.
tasks.human_edge: State what the evidence supports and resist premature conclusions.
tasks.altitude: Reduce evidence transcription and prose preparation while preserving investigator conclusions.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: source-linked exports and bounded drafting can support report preparation; security conclusions still need evidence review.

assumptions: Provisional shares concern an internal report, including filing and sending. Regulatory or customer disclosure requires separate authority and receives no savings credit here.

Investigators already produce case_id, event_id, timestamp, timezone, asset_id, observation, source_reference and verification_status in the case store. s1 retains selecting/validating evidence; absent structured evidence, manually prepare tables and deduct that effort before claiming benefit.
Try the existing case-system report export first. s2 copies verified observations only and preserves timezone and source reference; it never labels an event an established cause.

s4's retained 11 hours includes reading and correction; s5 keeps the existing full final review. a1/a2 bind report hash, redactions, storage access and recipient list after the final version exists; changes invalidate both. Separate save and delivery permissions are required.
unknowns: Current manual table and filing effort
research_questions: Can reviewers trace every statement in the report to evidence without losing uncertainty or timestamps?

already_counted.description: Read and correct generated case prose

incremental.description: Maintain report mapping and check confidential-data boundaries

approvals.approved_version: s5 final report hash, redactions and storage access
s5 final report hash and recipient list

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 15 table, 9 prose and 5 file/send hours minus 2 upkeep = 27. Low has native table/export and delivery already, leaving 9 prose minus 2 upkeep = 7. No investigation time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Support users installing and using security products.

steps.what: Clarify the user's security product installation or use problem
Inspect authorised product diagnostics and select the supported procedure
Provide technical support and demonstrate the selected security product procedure
Approve the complete endpoint action and its exact target
Apply the approved security product installation or setting change
Verify product operation and confirm the user's problem is resolved
Write and check the support outcome note
Commit the checked security support note

tasks.design: Configure the existing endpoint-management console in {OTHER} to show approved diagnostics and run signed standard actions. Keep the live support conversation, procedure selection and successful-use check human. Review the actual action and endpoint before executing it. Capture the support note in {HELPDESK} and approve its completed content before a separate commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support depends on the user's actual endpoint state, product version and ability to follow safe instructions.
tasks.enabler_now: A native endpoint console can expose diagnostics and execute a precisely selected signed procedure.
tasks.still_hard: A technically successful install can still leave the user unable to work or disable an important protection.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the protection and adapt the demonstration to the user's understanding.
tasks.altitude: Reduce diagnostic navigation and approved action execution, retaining live user support.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: managed endpoint consoles can show product status and execute approved installation actions; exact access and product support need validation.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for an internal managed-endpoint support case. User conversation remains full time. Already automated deployment or diagnostics earn no new savings.

s1 engineer captures ticket_id, endpoint_id, product_version, requested_action and symptom; s2 reads the endpoint agent's status, error_code, policy_version and diagnostic_timestamp. Missing or unmanaged endpoints use manual support, with no automatic action.

s2 retains interpretation and procedure selection. s4 checks the complete signed package or setting diff, endpoint_id, privileges and recovery procedure after the plan exists. a1 is revoked if target, package or settings change; nonstandard scripts require a new review.

s7 engineer captures action_id, result, verification and unresolved_issue; capture time stays full. a2 binds the finished note and ticket. No model receives endpoint credentials and no external user messages are sent.
unknowns: Current hands-on diagnostic and installation effort
research_questions: Which standard product actions are safe and reversible for the supported endpoint population?

incremental.description: Keep product procedures and endpoint action permissions current

approvals.approved_version: s4 exact signed action, settings and endpoint identifier
s7 checked note and ticket identifier

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 5 diagnostic navigation, 10 hands-on application and 2 note-commit hours minus 2 upkeep = 15. Low keeps installation and save manual, saving 5 minus 2 = 3. Guidance, approval, verification and note capture retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use bounded drafting and native security tooling while retaining threat judgement, evidence conclusions and operational authority.
reach: Help security operations define independently testable detection changes and evidence-linked reports.
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who turns investigated threats into tested controls and clear reports with explicit authority for each production change.
